title: Vice-President addresses Orientation Programme for Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly in Bhubaneswar
subtitle:
Vice-President urges legislators to uphold democratic values and strengthen public trust through dedicated service
Healthy debate, constructive cooperation essential for strengthening democracy: Vice-President
Vice-President calls for greater use of AI and digital technologies in legislative functioning
Odisha’s progress will be central to India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047: Vice-President
body_text:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today addressed the Orientation Programme for the Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly in Bhubaneswar. Calling upon legislators to uphold the rich democratic traditions of Bharat, he emphasised the importance of constructive debates, informed discussions, legislative efficiency and people-centric governance in strengthening democratic institutions. Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan addressed the Orientation Programme for the Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly in Bhubaneswar today.

He emphasised the importance of constructive debates, informed discussions, adherence to legislative procedures and embracing emerging technologies to strengthen democratic institutions. He urged legislators to uphold Bharat’s rich democratic traditions and work towards a developed Odisha, contributing to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

Governor of Odisha, Shri Braj Mohan Ram; Chief Minister, Shri Mohan Charan Majhi; Speaker of the Odisha Legislative Assembly, Smt. Surama Padhy;along with Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly were present on the occasion. — Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 16, 2026 The Vice-President appreciated the Speaker, Smt. Surama Padhy, for organising the orientation programme, describing such initiatives as instrumental in strengthening democratic institutions and enabling legislators to discharge their constitutional responsibilities effectively. Referring to India’s ancient democratic traditions, the Vice-President cited the democratic institutions of Vaishali and the Chola-era Kudavolai system, observing that democracy has deep roots in Bharat’s civilisational history. He said that Bharat rightly takes pride in being the ‘Mother of Democracy’ and called upon the legislators of Odisha to live up to this distinguished legacy. Emphasising that electoral victories must translate into meaningful public service, the Vice-President said, “We win in the elections by votes, but we can earn the respect of the people only through our service." He observed that the Legislative Assembly is much more than a forum for debate, as every policy framed, question raised and law enacted has the potential to improve the lives of countless citizens. Referring to the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, he said that Odisha’s progress would be central to India’s progress. With Odisha approaching the centenary of its formation as a province in 2036, he highlighted the significance of Vision Odisha 2036 in transforming the State into a developed, prosperous and inclusive State. He expressed confidence that legislators would play an important role in creating opportunities for the youth and ensuring that development reaches every village and every family. Addressing the issue of disruptions in legislative proceedings, the Vice-President emphasised that differences of opinion should not come in the way of the larger commitment to the people and the Constitution. He remarked, “In a democracy, we may agree to disagree, but we should all agree towards one thing – our commitment to the people and the Constitution.” Reiterating that “debate, discussion or even sometimes disruption must lead to a decision”, he called for healthy debates and constructive cooperation to strengthen democracy and advance national development. Underscoring the importance of continuous learning and preparation, the Vice-President urged Members to familiarise themselves thoroughly with legislative rules and procedures, budgetary processes, committee systems, parliamentary conventions and ethics. He particularly highlighted the importance of Question Hour and Zero Hour, describing them as crucial opportunities for individual Members to raise constituency-related concerns and important policy matters. He urged Members to cooperate with the Chair to ensure that these important parliamentary instruments function without disruption. The Vice-President also emphasised the role of the Business Advisory Committee (BAC) in building consensus on the business of the House. He observed that greater agreement within the Committee would contribute to smoother and more productive legislative proceedings. Highlighting the growing role of technology in legislative functioning, the Vice-President welcomed the inauguration of the Digital House in the Odisha Legislative Assembly under the National e-Vidhan Application. Referring to the increasing use of digital platforms in the Rajya Sabha, he noted that parliamentary papers, questions and debates were now available in multiple languages with the support of technology. He urged legislators to embrace emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing, to make legislative institutions future-ready. Concluding his address, the Vice-President reminded legislators of the immense responsibility and transformative potential of their office. He observed that a thoughtful intervention could bring about a change in policy, while a compassionate decision could restore hope in the lives of countless citizens. He wished all Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly a fruitful orientation programme and an enriching legislative journey. The programme was attended by Governor of Odisha, Shri Braj Mohan Ram; Chief Minister of Odisha, Shri Mohan Charan Majhi; Speaker of the Odisha Legislative Assembly,Smt. Surama Padhy; Deputy Speaker of Odisha Legislative Assembly Shri Bhabani Shankar Bhoi; and Members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly, among other dignitaries. *** PR/ASM/VM
